title: Triangle Clue Finder
prompt: Click a marker to reveal the fact that a careful student should notice in the triangle.

props.imageAlt: Triangle diagram with labeled parts and reminders

hotspots.label: Right-angle clue
hotspots.content: The square marker tells you one angle is **90°**. That means the side across from it is the hypotenuse, and the Pythagorean theorem may be useful.

hotspots.label: Height clue
hotspots.content: The height is the **perpendicular distance** to the base. It is the measurement you need for triangle area, even when another side looks easier to use.

hotspots.label: Hypotenuse clue
hotspots.content: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right triangle. It is always opposite the right angle.

hotspots.label: Angle-sum clue
hotspots.content: Every triangle has interior angles that add to **180°**. If two angles are known, the third one is fixed.

fallback.markdown: A triangle diagram usually gives you more than one clue. Look for a right-angle marker, a perpendicular height, the side opposite the right angle, and the rule that all triangle angles sum to $180^\circ$.
